request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A button downloads the policy versions as a CSV file: a header line

agent.result_text:
I added the policy export button, and the test that checks it (`policy export`) passes. Overall, `bin/e2e` ran 4 tests: 3 passed and 1 failed. The failure is in a part of the app I didn't touch, and I've left it unfixed.

**The change.** It's all in one front-end file, `src/main/frontend/features/policy/policy.slot.tsx`. A new **Export policy versions (CSV)** button (`data-testid="export-policy"`) sits under the policy viewer. When pressed, it re-reads the settings, people, claims and rates from the server, then downloads `policy.csv`:
- The header is `version,from,key,value,claims,due-total`, followed by one line per version, oldest first.
- **claims** is how many claims are dated while that version is in force, using the same rule the policy viewer already uses.
- **due-total** adds up the dues of only those claims that count toward totals (open, pending or settled ones, not drafts or voided). Each due is worked out the same way as the claim's due column.

No server, schema or audit changes were needed.

**The failure: "policy export scenario 2"** (`e2e/specs/acceptance.spec.ts:947`). The user `vic` has the `restricted` role, and the sheet's `perm-close` setting is `clerk`. The test expects vic's soft-close of period `2026-04` to be refused. The app allows it and writes `PERIOD_SOFT_CLOSED ... by=vic period=2026-04`, while the test's expected audit lines have no such line.

The cause is `Settings.permits` (`src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/setting/Settings.java`). It deliberately treats a restricted user as a clerk ("A restricted user may do what a clerk may"), so the soft-close goes through. The test implies some rule that should refuse it, and I can't tell which one is meant. Three possibilities:
- A restricted user isn't covered when the permission setting names only `clerk`.
- A period that hasn't started yet (today is 2026-03-25) can't be soft-closed.
- A period in a later financial year can't be soft-closed.

Guessing would change permissions or period rules across the app, so I didn't. If you tell me which rule is intended, I'll put it in and rerun the tests.

probe.probe_text:
# What the sheet shows and the rules behind it Nothing was changed. One thing to know before the list: **every figure on the screen is calculated in the browser**, mainly in `frontend/features/rates/ratesQuery.ts` and `claims/claimsQuery.ts`. A separate Java version of the same maths (`rollup/Rollup.java` and `setting/Settings.java`) produces the audit lines, period closes, snapshots and the figure frozen when a claim is settled. I compared the two copies and they don't always agree (notes at the end). ## 1. Figures and rules ### Per claim (claim row) - **`claim-due`** comes from `figure()` in the browser, or `Rollup.figure` plus `Settings.withLate` in Java. It is worked out in this order: 1. If the claim has a `settledDue` (frozen at settle), that is the figure. 2. Otherwise, if a statement bound it (`stated`), the figure is `statedDue`. 3. Otherwise it is the live figure: amount × the rate of the grade the person had **on the claim's date** (`gradeOn`), shown as "n/a" if there is no rate. - **Rate** (`rateFor` / `Rates.forClaim`): the rate with the latest from-date on or before the claim's date. It doesn't apply after its own to-date, and an older rate doesn't take over again. If the sheet has no rate, the parent sheet's is used, then the grandparent's (up to `PARENT_LEVELS`), then the sheet it was cloned from (`level`, `lineage`). A forward-only rate (`claimsAfter`) applies only to claims added after it was saved. - **Rounding** (`roundsHalfUp` / `Settings.rounding`): the dated `rounding` setting on the claim's date. If none is set, claims dated before the `policy-date` round half-up and the rest round half-even. A correction rounds by the date of the claim it corrects. - **Floor** (`floored`): the figure is raised to the dated `floor` on the claim's date (default 1.00). Corrections have no floor. - **Late charge** (`lateAdded` / `lateMonths`): applies while the claim is overdue. For each full 30 days from `overdueFrom`, it adds `late-pct` (as set on that 30-day boundary date) of the running total, compounding and rounded like the claim. There is no late charge for a correction, a deferred claim, or (in Java only) a `waived` claim. The charge keeps growing with the sheet's today. - **`claim-due-by`**: fixed when the claim is made, as the terms-th **business day** after its date (`Holidays.dueBy` / `businessDays`, which skips weekends and the sheet's holidays). - Terms come from `Person.termsNow`: the person's own dated terms, else their grade's `terms-`, else the sheet's `terms` (default 14). All are read **as of the sheet's today**, not the claim's date. - `due_terms` is stored with the claim. Adding a holiday calls `Claims.refixDueBys` for claims not SETTLED/VOID/DELETED that are due on or after it. - A steward's `setDueBy` drops the terms, so holidays no longer move that date. - Re-dating a claim keeps its due-by. - **`claim-overdue`** (`isOverdue` / `Settings.overdue`): yes when the claim is OPEN or PENDING, not deferred, and `overdueFrom` (due-by + `grace-` days, using the grade on the claim's date) is before today. - **`claim-period`** (`periodOf`): the period that **contains the due-by**, not the claim's date. - **`claim-number`** (`Claims.changeStatus` / `number`): given on SETTLED (or approval) and never reused. - The format is `FY-` from one sequence shared across the sheet's tree, using the fiscal year of the due-by (`fiscal-start-month`). - While `period-numbering-from` is reached, it is `-` instead, or `X-` when the due-by is in no period. - Reassigning a claim renumbers it (`reassign`). Transfer and clone renumber too. - **`claim-stated`, `claim-late-entry`, `claim-deferred`/`-until`, `claim-held`, `claim-waived`, `claim-proofs` (`-receipt`/`-photo`), `claim-split-from`, `claim-opened-by`, `claim-reminded`, `claim-batch`, `claim-review-user`**: stored flags or values shown as they are. Two of them are worked out: - `lateEntry`: true when the claim was added while its due-by was in a soft-closed period (`Claims.lateEntry`). - `isDeferred`: an OPEN or SETTLED claim, not stated, before `deferredUntil`. - **`claim-review-late` / `claim-pending-late`** (`isReviewLate`, `isPendingLate`): `reviewOn`/`pendingOn` + `review-sla`/`pending-sla` days is before today. - **`claim-policy`**: the policy version in force on the claim's date (`policyOn`; every save of a `POLICY` setting is a new version). ### Which claims count (`counts` / `Rollup.counts`) - Only OPEN, PENDING (`isOpen`) and SETTLED claims count. DRAFT, VOID, DELETED and REVIEW never do. - A claim deferred on today doesn't count. - An open claim of a person whose `retiredFrom` has been reached doesn't count, unless a statement bound it (`stated`). - **Holds** (person or claim) leave nothing out in the code. They only remove the person's pool cut while held on today. - A claim shared with others (`shares`) counts for each holder: `holderPart` = amount × share% × the rate of the holder's own grade. A settled claim's parts are its frozen due × share. The owner counts the remainder (`personPart`). ### Per person (person row) - **`person-claimed`**: sum of the amounts of counting claims that are not corrections (`corrects === null`). - **`person-due-total`** (`personDue` = `personSum` → `capped`): - It adds up what the person counts of every counting claim, skipping n/a. - It shows "n/a" when there is no rate for their grade today and no figure. - It is capped at `cap` less their pool cut total (not below 0). The cap used is the one in force on the date of their **latest counting claim** (`useCapFor` / `Settings.capped`). - **`person-excess`**: how much the uncapped sum is above that cap. - **`person-settled-total` / `person-open-total`** (`settledAndOpen`): the same parts, split by status and not capped. - **`person-aged-0-30`, `-31-60`, `-61`** (`agedDue`): open counting figures bucketed by days from the **claim's date** to today. - **`person-overdue-count` / `person-overdue-total`**: counting claims that are overdue, and their full figures. - **`person-score`** (`score`): the settled total with corrections left out ÷ 100, minus 5 per overdue claim, rounded half-even. - **`person-band`**: HIGH or MID or LOW against `score-high`/`score-mid`, blank unless both are set. - **`person-backing`** (`recentSettled`, `sumOfShares`): for each patron, their frozen SETTLED figures dated in the last 90 days × the patron's share%. - **`person-cut-total`** (`PoolCuts.totals`): their live pot cuts across pools. - A pool only gives cuts when its shares add up to exactly 100.00 and the sheet has a `pot`. - A retired member's share counts as 0. - A member held on today gets no cut, and their share is spread over the others. - **`person-period-

-due-total`** (`personPeriodDue` / `Rollup.personDueTotals`): figures of claims whose due-by is in the period and that counted by the status their log shows at the end of the period's last day (`statusOn` / `statusesOn`). Once the period is closed or soft-closed, it shows the fixed `personTotals`. - **`person-period-

-carried`** (`personCarried`): claims belonging to earlier periods that were still open at their end, plus `period_person_opening` (opening balances from the openings import or a rollover). - **`person-active`** (`isActive`): has an open counting claim dated in the last 30 days. - **`person-claims--count`**: a plain count of claims by status. - **`person-flag-shown`**: the flag reason while today ≤ `until`. - **Statement figures** (`person-stated-total`, `-count`, `-date`): a statement records the person's due-total and binds each counting claim at its current figure (`Claims.bind`). `unstate` (steward only) releases them. - **Other person values**: `person-grade` is `gradeOn(today)`, `person-terms` is `ownTermsOn(today)`, and `person-retired`, `held` and `holds` are as stored. ### Sheet totals - **`header-due-total`, `-overdue-total`, `rollup-*`, settled/open totals** use `trimmedSum`: with three or more people, the single highest and lowest are dropped. - **Claimed total and aged totals** are not trimmed. - **Grade summary** leaves out retired people. ### What is frozen, and when - **Settle / approve** freezes `settledDue`: the bound statement figure if there is one, otherwise the live figure with today's late charge, or the as-of figure for a settle as of a date (`ApplyClaimStatus`). - `resettle` (steward only) re-freezes at today's live figure. - **A statement** freezes `statedDue` per claim until it is unstated. Reassign, split and merge unbind the claims they move. - **Close / soft-close / auto-close** fixes each person's period due-total, the carried figure, the period total and the pool cuts (`ClosePeriod`, `SoftClosePeriod`, `PoolCuts.fix`). - Auto-close happens on a today change when to-date + `grace-days` is before the new today (`AutoClosePeriods`). - Reopen (steward only) makes them live again. A **locked** period can't be reopened. - **A closed period** (by due-by, `closedOn`) refuses adding a claim whose due-by would land in it, and refuses editing, opening, settling, voiding, deferring, proofing, re-dating or resettling its claims. - **A soft close** fixes the figures but leaves claims editable. New claims get marked `lateEntry`. - **A today change** writes a SNAPSHOT (each person's due-total), a SCORE line if the score log is on, and releases all claim locks. ### Status and who may do what - **Transitions** (`ClaimStatus.allows`): - DRAFT→OPEN, or DRAFT→REVIEW when the due is above `review-threshold`. - OPEN→SETTLED, or OPEN→PENDING when a clerk settles above the clerk limit (`clerkLimit`, the grade's own first). - PENDING→SETTLED (approve) or PENDING→OPEN (reject, which needs a reason). - REVIEW→OPEN by a steward's "review". - DRAFT, OPEN, PENDING or REVIEW→VOID. SETTLED→VOID by a steward only, within `VOID_SETTLED_DAYS` = 7 days of settling. - DRAFT↔DELETED, with restore allowed only on the same today the claim was deleted. - **Roles** (`Settings.role`, `permits`): - Clerk is the default. `viewer` may change nothing. `restricted` acts as a clerk but sees only their crews in the people list. A delegation makes someone a steward for its dates. - The perm matrix keys are `perm-open|settle|void|reassign|close|reopen|today`. By default reassign and reopen are steward-only and the rest are clerk or steward. - **Steward only**: approve and reject (or the person's approver), review, waive, set due-by, re-date, reassign, resettle, lock and unlock, merge, transfer, flag, unstate, rollover, withdraw rate, archive, clone. - **Four eyes**: the opener and the last editor can't settle or approve a claim. For a part-settle this is judged on the original claim. - **Opening refused when**: - the person is flagged and the user isn't a steward; - the period's `cap` on open claims is reached (`openInPeriod`), or `max-open` is reached; - the due is above `note-threshold` and the claim has no note. - **Settling refused when** the due is above `proof-threshold` (the grade's own first) without a proof, or without one of each `proof-kinds`. A deferred claim can't be settled. - **Retirement**: no claim may be dated after `retiredFrom`, or strictly inside a past retirement (`RefuseRetiredInput`). - **Other edit rules**: only a DRAFT is editable, and only while its editor isn't locked by someone else (`ClaimLocks`). A claim with lines must equal the sum of its lines. - **Corrections**: a negative amount must name a SETTLED claim of the same person (`RefuseInvalidCorrection`). It is left out of claimed and the score, but its due counts. ### Imports and other bulk actions - **People import**: matches by name or alias to update, otherwise adds. A blank grade gets `default-grade`. All or nothing. - **Paste**: adds and opens one claim per line, or updates a matching DRAFT. All or nothing. - **Openings import**: adds to the opening balance, which feeds the carried figure. - **Rate import**: works like the rate form. - **Rollover**: makes the next fiscal year's periods, carries each person's open figure into the first new period's opening, and soft-closes the old year. - I read the paste, import, merge and transfer rules from their YAML header comments rather than tracing their code in full. ## 2. How hard this was to find and follow It was hard. The logic is scattered and in several places contradicts itself: - The screen's figures are calculated in the browser, and the same maths is copied in Java (`Rollup`, `Settings`, `ApplyClaimStatus.due`). The rules are spread over about 150 tiny step classes, the YAML header comments, and long javadoc that often disagrees with the code. - **Holds:** the hold YAMLs and the `Claim.held` javadoc say a held claim counts in no live total. `Person`, `Rollup.counts` and `counts()` in the browser say holds only affect pool cuts, and nothing ever reads `claim.held` in a total. - **Waive:** the server honours `waived` in the late charge, but `figure()` in the browser doesn't. So a waived overdue claim shows a late charge on screen but is frozen without one when settled. - **Numbering:** the browser's `Claim` type says a number is given on opening; the server gives it on settle. - **Terms:** comments say "days" and "the grade on the claim's date", but the code uses business days and the terms in force on today. - **Closing:** the close YAMLs say "claims dated in" the period, but the code uses the due-by. A new developer would have to read both the TypeScript and the Java versions, and couldn't trust the comments.
